authority: apostila-cga-2026; exhaustive sweep of all 59 corpus occurrences of `liquidez`
method: every occurrence of `liquidez` read in context; every occurrence of `benchmarks` read in context
reason: The single largest recall defect in the registry: `liquidez` occurs 59 times and matched NOTHING, because risk.liquidity and technical.liquidity both claimed it and the collision demoter sent both to review. Demotion was the wrong resolution — the two claims are not equally good. Read exhaustively, the risk sense NEVER appears on the bare surface: all ten risk occurrences carry `risco de`, which risk.liquidity already owns as an automatic form. So the claim to remove is risk.liquidity's, and this is exactly the case the campaign learned in round one — a review claim dominates an automatic mapping by design, so demoting the wrong claimant is not enough, it has to go.

operations.why: Bare `liquidez` is the property, not the risk, in 49 of 59 occurrences — `com grande liquidez`, `baixa liquidez`, `a liquidez da carteira`. The other 10 all read `risco de liquidez` or `gestão do risco de liquidez`, which the concept keeps as automatic forms and which win by length. Removing rather than demoting because a review claim suppresses the automatic mapping that owns the surface.

With risk.liquidity's claim gone the surface is uncontested. The 10 risk occurrences are consumed by the longer `risco de liquidez`, and `gestão de liquidez`, `prêmio pela liquidez` and `preferência pela liquidez` take theirs the same way — which is what global longest-match now guarantees and the old leftmost scan did not.
20 occurrences of the plural against 104 of the singular, which is automatic. `Tipos de Benchmarks` heads a section and matched nothing at all.
Same surface, same sense; the corpus is bilingual and the form is shared.
